item.title: The Kennedy Center names new artistic director, amid concerns
item.description: The center's executive director has named an agent who has worked with ZZ Top and Motley Crue drummer Tommy Lee as the head of programming for the arts institution.

item.title: At least 2 deaths attributed to Isaias after hurricane bashes Florida and Alabama
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is blamed for at least two deaths, after the storm made landfall on the Florida coast and ran through Alabama. There are numerous reports of downed trees, with hundreds of thousands of people without power.

item.title: Parallel parking is now a sport in Philly, complete with speed and flair
item.description: Philadelphia recently held its first-ever Parallel Parking Association Championship. Hundreds of people came out to see drivers compete for speed, accuracy and even flair.

item.title: How a retired Navajo Nation doctor earned a MacArthur 'genius' grant for public art
item.description: Chip Thomas, a retired physician on the Navajo Reservation, is well known for his large photograhpic murals. Now, he's been recognized with a MacArthur "genius" grant.

item.title: ICE shooting in NYC fuels tension between New York officials and Trump administration
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement shot a man in New York City. It raised tensions between the Trump administration and New York officials over the state's sanctuary policies.

item.title: The U.S. last held a public execution in the 1930s. The Pentagon wants to change that
item.description: The Pentagon says it will livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan at Fort Hood, the site of his 2009 mass shooting. That would be the first public execution in the U.S. since the 1930s.
item.content:encoded:
